label: CJEU C-362/14 — Schrems v Data Protection Commissioner (Schrems I)
body: 1. An adequacy decision adopted by the Commission does not prevent a national supervisory authority from examining a complaint that a third country does not ensure an adequate level of protection. National SAs retain competence; only the Court of Justice can declare a Commission decision invalid.
2. Commission Decision 2000/520 (the US-EU Safe Harbor) is invalid.
Why it matters: Established the "essentially equivalent" standard for third-country protection and the principle that national SAs are independent gatekeepers. Set the stage for Schrems II.
